content.text: The text chiefly recounts Dr. Elsie Inglis’s humanitarian career. After founding the Scottish Women’s Hospitals, she travelled to Serbia in 1915, treating typhus and wounded soldiers at Kragujevatz, Valjevo, Mladenovatz, Lazarevatz, and Krushieevatz. During the Austro-German invasion she remained with Serbian patients, endured captivity, and eventually travelled through Vienna and Bludenz to Zürich. In 1916–17 she led a women’s unit via Archangel and Moscow to Odessa, then served at Medgidia, Braila, Galatz, and Reni during the Romanian retreat and Russian Revolution. She evacuated with Serbian forces, travelling from Hadji Abdul through Russia to Archangel and Newcastle. Seriously ill, Inglis died soon after reaching Newcastle and was buried in Edinburgh, honoured by Scotland and Serbia. The text also contains unrelated excerpts about African adventures and Parisian student life.
